courthouses.name: Fresno Superior Courthouse — Downtown Location
courthouses.hours: Clerk's Office 8:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m.; building Mon–Fri 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.
courthouses.note: Court lists case types as Criminal and Juvenile Dependency. Main downtown criminal courthouse. Court notes Drug Court is currently heard at the M Street Courthouse.

courthouses.name: Jail Annex — Criminal Courts Departments 95 & 96
courthouses.note: Court lists case types as Criminal and Domestic Violence. Same street address the Sheriff gives for the North Annex Jail. Court advises arranging childcare if you have business here.

courthouses.name: "M" Street Courthouse
courthouses.hours: Clerk's Office Mon–Fri 8:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m.; building Mon–Fri 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.
courthouses.note: Court lists criminal infractions and traffic infractions. Drug Court is currently heard here (per the Downtown listing).

courthouses.name: ACTION Center (After Criminal One-Stop Network)
courthouses.address: 1100 Van Ness Avenue (first-floor room behind Jury Assembly Room)
courthouses.note: Not a courtroom: post-sentencing service window. Processes criminal sentencing orders — Adult Offender Work Program, Adult Theft Diversion, anger management, batterer's treatment, DV review, community service, drug testing, DUI classes, electronic monitoring, fines.

courthouses.name: Juvenile Justice Court
courthouses.note: Juvenile delinquency (misdemeanor and felony) and juvenile drug court only — not adult criminal.

courthouses.name: B. F. Sisk Courthouse
courthouses.hours: Clerk's Office Mon–Thu 8:00 a.m.–3:00 p.m., Fri 8:00 a.m.–12:00 p.m.
courthouses.note: Civil, probate, family law, restraining orders, small claims, unlawful detainer, Self-Help Center. Not criminal.

courthouses.name: Archives Facility
courthouses.hours: Clerk: Mon & Wed 8:00 a.m.–3:00 p.m., Fri 8:00 a.m.–12:00 p.m.
courthouses.note: Records storage and old case files; no hearings.

legal_aid.name: Fresno County Public Defender — Clean Slate Program
legal_aid.serves: People with Fresno County convictions (or probation transferred to and completed in Fresno County), off probation/parole, with no open cases
legal_aid.what: Free post-conviction record relief: dismissals/expungement, felony reductions, Prop 47 and Prop 64. Requires a DOJ Live Scan record first; apply online or on paper; appointment-only, no walk-ins; review can take up to 12 months.
legal_aid.address: 2135 Fresno Street, Suite 100, Fresno, CA 93721 (lobby 8–12 and 1–4)
legal_aid.todo: PD contact page instead lists 'Clean Slate Program @ Fresno EOC', 1805 E California Ave, (559) 263-8915, cleanslate@co.fresno.ca.us — conflicts with the Clean Slate page; confirm before going

legal_aid.name: Fresno Superior Court Self-Help Service Center (Centro de Recursos Legales)
legal_aid.what: Forms help and information mainly for civil/family cases; gives information, not legal advice. Walk-in Mon 9–2, Tue & Wed 9–1; phone/email Thu & Fri 9–3.
legal_aid.address: 1130 O Street, First Floor, Fresno, CA 93724

programs.name: Pretrial Release Program (Probation)
programs.summary: Probation uses a validated risk tool to help the court decide release at arraignment, then monitors released people so they make court dates. Can refer to free services (Day Reporting Center, substance use and mental health treatment, CBT classes, transitional housing, job training). No cost; GPS only if ordered by the court or at Probation's discretion.

programs.name: Collaborative (Treatment) Courts
programs.summary: Court says it runs seven treatment courts combining judicial oversight, regular hearings, intensive supervision and sanctions/incentives. Pages listed include Behavioral Health Court, DUI Court, Mental Health (AB 1810) Court, Unity Court, Veterans Treatment Court, Family Behavioral Health Court and the CARE Act. Ask your attorney about eligibility.

programs.name: Mental Health Diversion (AB 1810 / SB 215)
programs.summary: The court's Criminal page notes people with qualifying mental disorders may be eligible for Mental Health Diversion if they meet the statutory criteria. Raise it with your attorney.

programs.name: ACTION Center
programs.summary: Go here if the court ordered you to complete a program (work program, theft diversion, anger management, batterer's treatment, community service, drug testing, DUI classes, electronic monitoring) or pay a fine. 1100 Van Ness Ave, first floor behind Jury Assembly Room; Mon–Fri 8–4.

jails.court_ids_note: Nearest criminal courtrooms (Depts 95 & 96 at 1265 M St, and 1100 Van Ness). Not confirmed which court in-custody defendants are taken to.

bail.note: Before paying a bail agent, check that their license is active using the California Department of Insurance license lookup (search by name or license number). Fresno Superior Court posts its bail schedules at https://www.fresno.courts.ca.gov/divisions/criminal/bail-schedules. Inmate account deposits go only through TouchPay (jail lobby kiosks, touchpaydirect.com, or 1-866-232-1899; facility number 293721 plus booking number); checks and money orders are not accepted. For custody status call (559) 600-8600 or (559) 475-9491. This is information only, not legal advice.
